mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent district court registry office under the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea, accessed through the I-ROS electronic registration system
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public followed by an Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (MOFA) if the destination state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; for a non-member state, use only MOFA consular authentication followed by legalization by the destination embassy or consulate in Seoul. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Corporate Status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District court registry office of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Korean notary public followed by Apostille certification by MOFA for Apostille Convention destinations; for non-Apostille destinations, MOFA consular authentication and then embassy or consulate legalization of the destination state. Apostille and consular legalization are never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing incorporation and granting Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized board resolution followed by MOFA Apostille for Apostille Convention states; for non-member states, MOFA consular authentication and destination mission legalization. The two authentication regimes are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan) as notarized and registered
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators and Board of Directors, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by MOFA Apostille for Hague Apostille states; for non-member states, MOFA consular authentication plus destination embassy or consulate legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel routes and must not be applied in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean licensed commercial bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean bank licensed under the Financial Holding Companies Act, including Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank or Hana Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank reference letter issued on bank letterhead, notarized by a Korean notary, then authenticated by MOFA Apostille for Apostille states; for non-Apostille states, MOFA consular authentication followed by legalization at the destination embassy or consulate in Seoul. Do not add consular legalization to an Apostille.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all direct shareholders, indirect owners, directors, officers, authorized signatories and ultimate beneficial owners against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit watchlist, Financial Services Commission administrative sanctions list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, US OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, UK Treasury consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated sanctions list, Interpol notices and domestic commercial PEP databases. Any PEP, including foreign, domestic or international-organization PEP, and their family members and close associates require enhanced due diligence, beneficial-ownership verification, senior-management approval and ongoing transaction monitoring. Suspicious transactions and named sanction matches shall be reported to KoFIU within three business days under FTRA, with customer due diligence refreshed annually or upon any ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Supreme Court electronic Registration System (I-ROS) at iros.go.kr, including the commercial registration name search and name clearance module operated by the competent district court registry offices
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Commercial Act Articles 289 and 290, a Chusik Hoesa must have a Korean-language Hangul script name in the commercial registration system and may include an English registered transliteration. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) proprietary or distinctive word or coined element; (2) business object or activity descriptor; (3) corporate form suffix Chusik Hoesa or its abbreviation; and (4) administrative disambiguation suffix such as a region, numeral or branch identifier only to avoid identical names. Foreign names must be submitted as Korean phonetic transliteration with a certified transliteration table; the English name used in banking and contracts must match the registered transliterated English name. Chinese characters are not permitted in the statutory registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the registry will issue a written notice stating the legal basis and conflicting name. The applicant may within 14 days file a re-examination objection with the same district court registry office, attaching evidence that the distinctive element is not confusing, that the prohibited token has been pre-authorized, or that prior registrations have lapsed. If rejected again, an administrative lawsuit under the Administrative Litigation Act may be commenced in the Administrative Court within 90 days of service of the rejection decision. An injunction may preserve the application pending litigation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally accepted only as a correspondence address for a Korean Chusik Hoesa if the company maintains a separate actual business location for employees, records and bank due-diligence visits. The National Tax Service and municipal district tax offices may reject a virtual-office address as the principal place of business if no human activity, utility bills, lease contract, or business signage is verifiable. For the PropTech SaaS industry, VAT zero returns and digital service invoices often trigger address review. Korean banks under the Real Name Transactions Act generally refuse corporate current accounts for mail-only virtual offices and require a signed lease, office identification and an on-site visit. Accordingly, the registered office should be an administrative office service with utility and signage, not a mail-only mailbox.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) original lease or sublease agreement for the registered office; (2) utility bill in company name; (3) signage proving active occupation; (4) employee payroll and attendance records; (5) corporate seal, books, minutes and accounting records present at the address; (6) cloud infrastructure or SaaS product documentation; (7) VAT invoices and expense receipts under the company's tax identification number. Risk quantification: Low, under 10% per year, for a physical office with lease, utility and signage; Moderate, approximately 25% to 35% per year, for a virtual-only office during the first two tax years, rising if the address is shared with more than ten other entities, if VAT returns show no local expenditure, or if the National Tax Service receives a tip-off. Municipal district office inspections are less common than National Tax Service district tax office inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1001 of January 27, 1963, as amended; chapters on stock corporations), Articles 288, 289, 290, 295, 300, 306, 312, 316, 317, 329 and 332; Presidential Decree on Commercial Registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Office of the Seoul Central District Court, operating through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office for online filings; local district court registration office for the jurisdiction of the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (Chusik Hoesa) together with the certified Articles of Incorporation and all statutory attachment documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Korea abolished the statutory minimum paid-up capital for stock corporations effective after the 2009 amendment to the Commercial Act. The company may be incorporated with any consideration its shareholders agree to provide, provided that the aggregate issue price of the shares is fully paid before registration, the par value of each share is at least KRW 100, and contributions in kind are verified by a court-appointed inspector where required under Article 290. There is no blocked escrow account requirement at the national level; however, the paid-in capital must be deposited into a bank account in the company's name and must remain untouched until the incorporation registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that upon the completion of the incorporation registration of KR_CHUSIKHOESA as a Chusik Hoesa (stock company) under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, the first meeting of the Board of Directors, duly convened and constituted with a legal quorum of the directors elected at the inaugural general shareholders meeting, hereby adopts the following pro forma first board resolutions: FIRST: Subscription and Share Capital. The Board ratifies the completion of the stock subscription process for the initial share issuance, confirms that all subscription payments have been fully deposited into the company's capital account before registration, and records that the paid-in capital amount is consistent with the Articles of Incorporation. The Board directs that any in-kind contribution, if made, had been examined by a court-appointed inspector in accordance with Article 290 of the Commercial Act. The Chief Executive Officer is authorized to maintain the register of shareholders and to issue share certificates upon request. SECOND: Banking and Payment Authorization. The Board authorizes the opening of corporate bank and payment accounts at a licensed financial institution in Korea. The Chief Executive Officer, jointly with the Chief Financial Officer, may designate authorized signatories, apply for corporate financial cards, obtain online banking certificates, and connect approved payment rails including Stripe Billing and ACH Direct. For all transfers exceeding the equivalent of USD 25,000, the signatures of two statutory officers are required, and all transactions must be recorded in a manner suitable for external audit and the entity-level tax classification of the company. THIRD: Registered Office and Corporate Seal. The Board adopts the place stated in the Articles of Incorporation as the registered office, directs the posting of the corporate sign, and instructs that the corporate seal and seal certificate be registered with the competent court registration office. Any change of the registered office shall be resolved by the Board and filed with the court within the time limits prescribed by the Commercial Act. FOURTH: Statutory Officer Appointments. The Board confirms the appointment of the statutory directors and officers named in the inaugural shareholders meeting, including the Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer, and any internal directors. The Board delegates operational authority to the Chief Executive Officer for the ordinary course of the PropTech SaaS business, while reserving to the Board the approval of mergers, acquisition or disposal of material assets, issuance of additional shares, amendment of the Articles, dissolution, and any transaction with a value exceeding USD 100,000. FIFTH: Implementation. The Board resolves that the foregoing resolutions shall be immediately effective, that all officers are fully authorized to execute and deliver any appropriate agreements, certificates, filings, and payment instructions, and that the corporate secretary is directed to file all statutory notices with registration authorities as required by Korean law. This resolution shall remain effective until revoked by a subsequent board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation and Promoter Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public office in Korea appointed under the Certified Judicial Scriveners Act; subsequent filing via the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a complete set of Korean-language incorporation documents. Every promoter must execute the Articles of Incorporation, stating the company name, business purpose, registered office, issued and authorized shares, and issue price per share. Each promoter must personally present at a notary public office in Korea, prove identity with a passport or resident registration certificate, and declare that the establishment is lawful. The notary will certify the Articles or draft and notarize a deed of constitution. If any promoter is a non-resident corporation, its signatory must hold a notarized power of attorney. After certification, the promoters should not submit the registration until capital payment and statutory officer appointments are completed.
required_dossiers: Korean-language Articles of Incorporation signed by all promoters
Promoter passport or resident registration certificate
Notarized power of attorney for foreign corporate promoters
In-kind contribution inspection report by court-appointed appraiser if applicable
Certificate of capital subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification, correct the Articles or the identity documents and re-submit before the same notary or another notary in the same jurisdiction. If the Internet Registration Office rejects the instrument because of an incomplete purpose clause, revise the clause to clearly describe the PropTech rental screening SaaS scope and re-file the certified version without additional fee beyond the normal supplement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Payment, Share Subscription, and Bank Paid-In Capital Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed under the Korean Banking Act; the Formation Promoters and initial shareholder-subscribers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital subscription account in the Company's name at a commercial bank licensed under the Korean Banking Act, and transfer the total subscription proceeds into that account by each shareholder or promoter. For cash subscriptions, retain deposit slips and bank transfer records. For non-cash contributions, the court-appointed appraiser's inspection certificate must be completed before the payment deadline under Article 290 of the Commercial Act. After all subscription amounts are received, obtain a bank-issued certificate of capital deposit, verify that the balance is not withdrawn, and prepare the subscription list with each subscriber's name and number of shares. This evidence will be submitted to the inaugural shareholders meeting and the registration office.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of capital deposit or balance certificate
Share subscription application forms
Bank transfer records and deposit slips
Subscriber identity documents and remittance evidence
Court-appointed appraiser's in-kind contribution valuation report if applicable
Subscription list showing number of shares per subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays issuing the paid-in certificate, request a simple deposit balance certificate under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and provide the court with the account screenshot or passbook record. If a subscription payment is reversed before registration, collect the amount again and obtain a refreshed bank certificate before filing the incorporation registration application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inaugural General Shareholders Meeting and Appointment of Statutory Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Promoters and shareholders acting under the Commercial Act; minutes sealed and retained as corporate records at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the inaugural general shareholders meeting without delay after subscription is completed. The promoters must present the Articles of Incorporation, the paid-in capital certificate, and the promoter's establishment report to the shareholders. The shareholders will elect the first directors and, if the size of the company requires, a statutory auditor. Immediately after the shareholders meeting, the elected directors must hold the first board meeting and adopt the pro forma first board resolution on share capital confirmation, banking authorizations, registered office, and officer delegations. Prepare meeting minutes signed by the chairman and attendees, and preserve the minutes and proxies at the registered office. Foreign shareholders may participate by proxy under a notarized power of attorney.
required_dossiers: Notice or waiver of notice of the inaugural general shareholders meeting
Promoter report on establishment proceedings
Paid-in capital deposit certificate
In-kind contribution valuation report if applicable
Consent to appointment of each director and statutory auditor
Minutes of the inaugural general shareholders meeting
Minutes of the first board of directors meeting
Proxies and notarized powers of attorney for foreign shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an absentee vote or proxy challenge is raised, re-solicit written votes or postpone the meeting with a fresh notice. If minority shareholders allege procedural defect in director elections, call a supplementary shareholders meeting to ratify the election or elect substitute directors, then recast the first board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registration Office or the local district court registration office having jurisdiction over the registered office, through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for incorporation registration to the competent district court registration office no later than three weeks after the first board meeting. The online filing should include the certified Articles of Incorporation, certificate of paid-in capital, minutes of the inaugural shareholders meeting, minutes of the first board meeting, director identification data, and the filing agent's power of attorney. Pay the court registration tax and education surcharge online or by revenue stamp. The registration officer will verify that the statutory formalities were satisfied and issue the certificate of incorporation registration. The company acquires legal personality on this registration date. After receiving the certificate, confirm the assigned corporate number before proceeding to tax registration.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of notarized Articles of Incorporation
Application form for incorporation registration
Bank certificate of paid-in capital deposit
Minutes of the inaugural general shareholders meeting
Minutes of the first board of directors meeting
Certificate of personal seal of each director
Power of attorney for the filing agent if any
Receipt of payment of registration tax and education surcharge
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration officer issues a correction order, submit the requested supplementary evidence through the Internet Registration Office within the stated cure period. If the deficiency concerns notarization or bank certification, cure the defect by obtaining the missing instrument and attaching an explanatory cover letter before the legal deadline; otherwise, withdraw and re-file without losing the earlier payment credit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax Registration, Corporate Seal Registration, and Annual Governance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service local tax office; Court Registration Office for the corporate seal certificate; regional employment and labor office for social insurance and workplace establishment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after registration with the court, apply for business registration with the National Tax Service local tax office and register the corporate seal with the court. If the company maintains a physical office in Korea, file a workplace establishment report with the regional employment and labor office, enroll employees in the four major social insurance programs, and register for electronic tax invoices. No physical industrial or environmental license is required for the pure SaaS scope, but general fire and building code compliance documents for the office lease must be accessible. Prepare for ongoing governance by maintaining the shareholder register, directors minutes, and statutory corporate books at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration issued by the court
Corporate seal registration application
Business registration application form
Office lease agreement or proof of registered office facility
Director identification documents and passports
Employment and labor office workplace establishment report if employees are in Korea
Contact information of the local tax office and assigned corporate identifier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service rejects the business registration because the office location appears nominal or missing, provide a copy of the office lease and utility invoice, or amend the registered office to a genuine operational workspace. If the labor office questions the workplace size, submit a floor plan and the building occupancy certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. This formation concerns a pure digital PropTech SaaS platform under ISIC 6201 with no physical manufacturing, chemical process, assembly line, or warehousing operation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No separate industrial operating license is required solely for developing and operating the real estate rental screening cloud platform. If the company later engages in licensed real estate brokerage in Korea, a separate report or license under the Licensed Real Estate Agents Act would be necessary before that activity begins.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable. ISIC 6201 software and SaaS services do not trigger an Environmental Impact Assessment, Environmental Registration, or Exempt category because there is no physical industrial installation, land disturbance, or pollutant-generating facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. There are no measurable wastewater discharge thresholds, volatile organic compound emission limits, hazardous waste handling standards, or continuous emissions monitoring obligations arising solely from the PropTech rental screening service. General office waste disposal obligations and electrical safety standards under municipal rules apply to the ordinary office footprint.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial licensing. No civil defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or workplace safety clearance is required because the company does not operate a factory, warehouse, or chemical facility. The company must nevertheless comply with the Framework Act on Firefighting and the Building Act for its leased office premises, including maintaining fire extinguishers, unobstructed exits, an occupancy certificate for the floor, and general occupational safety measures for computer-based office work under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Nexus assessment: a Chusik Hoesa established in Korea must register for corporate income tax and VAT. A foreign non-resident entity that will carry on business or make VAT taxable supplies in Korea must also register with the National Tax Service (NTS). Step 2 - Tax representative: a foreign entity without a domestic place of business should appoint a resident tax agent authorized to receive legal process and file tax returns. Step 3 - Application: file the business registration application through the HomeTax portal or at the competent district tax office before commencing business, or within 20 days after business commencement. Step 4 - Documentary evidence: attach the certificate of foreign incorporation, articles of incorporation, proof of registered address, board resolution appointing the Korean tax agent, evidence of the Korean supply activity or place of business, and any written contracts with Korean counterparties. Step 5 - NTS review and issuance: after verification, the NTS issues the Business Registration Certificate containing the ten-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as the unified TIN and VAT identifier. Step 6 - Foreign e-commerce treatment: a non-resident digital service supplier without a Korean establishment must complete the special overseas e-commerce seller VAT registration track through HomeTax if it supplies qualifying digital services to Korean consumers; this produces a separate simplified VAT collection number. Step 7 - Post-registration: keep statutory books and records, file periodic VAT returns, and update the NTS portal with any changes in business identity. Foreign entities with no Korean source income and no VAT taxable transactions are not required to apply for a Korean TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box election for a domestic Chusik Hoesa; all domestic stock corporations are per se entity level taxable corporations. No hybrid mismatch election is available; OECD hybrid mismatch anti-abuse rules are applied mandatorily to deny double deductions or income exclusions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for a Chusik Hoesa; VAT registration is mandatory upon business commencement in Korea regardless of anticipated revenue. Simplified taxpayer status is available only to certain individual business operators with annual taxable turnover below KRW 30,000,000, and this concession does not apply to a corporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The NTS operates a mandatory electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) transmission system through HomeTax. Every VAT taxable supply made by a corporation must be evidenced by an e-tax invoice; paper tax invoices are permitted only in limited statutory cases. Transaction data is transmitted to the NTS via HomeTax, an approved EDI service provider, or a certified API integration using the NTS electronic tax invoice XML schema. Korea is not a pre-clearance stamping jurisdiction; there is no real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamp required before each transaction. Instead, the NTS performs automated cross-matching of issued and received e-tax invoices against VAT returns and issues automated mismatch correction requests. Missing or fraudulent e-tax invoice entries attract statutory surcharges, and false e-tax invoices can trigger criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, the export of goods is zero-rated when the goods leave Korea under a customs export declaration and are paid for in foreign currency. Services, including cloud-based PropTech SaaS subscriptions supplied to foreign clients, are zero-rated as export-of-services when they qualify as services that earn foreign currency or are performed for a non-resident under the statutory export-of-services categories; the supply must not be consumed or used in Korea, the beneficiary must be a non-resident, and the consideration must be received in convertible foreign currency. Domestic B2C supply or in-Korea use does not qualify. The taxpayer must substantiate the zero rate with the complete export documentation bundle and repatriated foreign exchange.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) for physical goods
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / multimodal transport document evidencing movement out of Korea
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / Foreign Exchange Bank Confirmation proving receipt of convertible foreign currency
Commercial invoice and international export contract with the foreign customer
For SaaS/service exports: signed offshore service agreement, detailed service description or completion report, customer non-residency evidence, and a HomeTax e-tax invoice marked zero-rated
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS will scrutinize export declarations, foreign exchange bank registers, shipping documents, and VAT refund claims. If zero-rating is applied but export proceeds are not repatriated within the 180-day statutory period, or the documentation bundle is incomplete, the NTS will retroactively reverse the zero rating and assess Korean VAT at 10% on the export consideration, plus late-payment interest and statutory additional tax for underreporting under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act. False e-tax invoices and forged customs documentation attract severe surcharges, including penalties up to a significant percentage of the invoiced amount, and criminal punishment under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act. Any input VAT previously refunded in connection with the disputed export is subject to full clawback and recovery.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), with policy authority for foreign exchange under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act jointly exercised by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Bank of Korea
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a broadly liberalised convertible currency regime for current-account transactions, such as trade settlements, dividends, royalties, and service fees, which may be settled in KRW or any foreign currency through a licensed foreign exchange bank without prior regulatory approval where the underlying transaction is properly documented and reported. Capital-account transactions, including inbound foreign equity investment, outward portfolio investment, lending, and borrowing, are subject to a standard declaration/reporting framework rather than a prior approval system for ordinary commercial transactions. Foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) is protected and generally enjoys full repatriation of capital and profits when the required notification has been made and the capital has been properly booked. The Korean won is convertible for settlement on the onshore KRW market; however, strict gatekeeping applies to non-residents in certain derivatives and speculative flows, and intraday foreign exchange positions are monitored by the Bank of Korea to curtail abnormal market pressure. A unified Foreign Exchange Information System monitors all cross-border settlements. Surrender requirements have been largely abolished, but each export transaction must be reported and settled through a domestic foreign exchange bank, and failure to repatriate export proceeds within the statutory timeline can trigger penalties, loss of foreign exchange bank status, and tax reporting consequences. Profit remittance requires evidence of paid-in capital, audited financial statements, tax clearance, and, if applicable, a foreign investment notification certificate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 99 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, Korean resident exporters must receive export proceeds within 180 days of the export declaration date. The exporter may apply in advance for an extension of up to an additional 180 days on reasonable commercial grounds. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; P. don't need this. However, the proceeds must be transferred into a domestic foreign exchange bank account or resident foreign currency deposit, and the export collection must be reported under the Export Collection Information System. Surrender is required only when the exporter elects to convert abroad? Actually, exporters must exchange or deposit within the required period; there is no current forced surrender rate. The conversion to KRW, if chosen, is executed at negotiated spot rates. Tolerance for loan? We'll leave.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs (e.g., Revolut, Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) are not licensed as banks under the Korean Banking Act and cannot open a direct corporate treasury account for a Korean Chusik Hoesa, because banking law requires that any entity providing multi-currency deposit-taking, payment, and settlement services to Korean residents hold a local financial license and maintain a branch in the Republic of Korea. As a result, the viability of deploying an offshore digital EMI as the primary liquidity rail is LOW. The only viable application is MEDIUM (restricted) where a major domestic bank acts as the designated settlement bank and the EMI operates as a white-label software front-end for invoicing, API payment orchestration, and reconciliation, while the underlying custody, capital verification, and FX conversion remain inside the licensed Korean bank. Even in that partner-banking structure, all outward remittances must flow through the local bank's SWIFT and foreign exchange reporting infrastructure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Real Identification Financial Transactions Act and the bank's own CDD policy, the statutory director or the officially appointed representative (either the foreign CEO or a locally resident director) must be physically present at a Korean branch to complete the new corporate account opening, sign the foreign investment capital escrow agreement, and undergo a live AML interview. Remote opening is not available as a default. However, several Tier-1 banks allow a consular proxy opening when the corporate record book, board resolution, apostilled power of attorney, original certificate of incorporation, passport copies of the ultimate beneficial owner, and the completed legal representative identity declaration are notarised and apostilled; the proxy appears in-branch, and a real-time video-KYC call is then scheduled with the foreign representative. Even then, the bank retains discretion to require a one-time physical visit for the signatory before activating outward international payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholders and dispersed nominee ownership create incomplete Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) identification on the initial corporate bank application.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarised UBO declaration, the full shareholder register, organisational chart of the investor chain, corporate registration certificates from each jurisdiction, identification documents (passport or national ID) of all natural persons holding 25% or more of voting rights, and a board resolution confirming the source of funds and purpose of the Korean entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The investors or counterparties come from high-risk jurisdictions or have negative media references, triggering enhanced due diligence and the compliance committee's jurisdiction screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a clean adverse-media and sanctions-screening report prepared by a reputable sources (e.g., World-Check / Dow Jones), audited statutory accounts of the parent company, bank reference letters from the parent's main banker for the past 12 months, passport-issued identification, proof of residential address, and a declaration of absence of politically exposed person (PEP) status for shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The PropTech SaaS billing model permits recurring subscription inflows and third-party B2B remittances, which can look like money laundering through layering if cross-border payment narratives are inconsistent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed business plan for the Korean entity, complete master SaaS contracts with end customers, sample invoice ledgers and billing history from the global parent, the initial capital expenditure forecast, transfer pricing documentation for the licensing of software/R&D into Korea, and a signed sworn statement that all funds received are sourced from legitimate business operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid round-tripping suspicion if capital is injected as foreign investment and immediately paid out as an intercompany loan or dividend in the first financial year.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a board-approved 13-month cash-flow treasury model, evidence of actual hiring expenditures and capital outlay (office leases, salaries, cloud infrastructure, local registration fees), audited financial projections, tax clearance certificate from the National Tax Service, and a CFO attestation explaining the business need for each major outbound payment category.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign direct investment into the Korean Chusik Hoesa must be reported to the Ministry of Economy and Finance through a domestic foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA). The wiring instruction should be transmitted via SWIFT MT103 from the overseas parent or investor to the Korean bank's beneficiary account, and must include the investor's full legal name, the Korean entity's business registration number, and a clean invoice narrative referencing the

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and applicable audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, file by March 31 of the following year. When the return is prepared by an external CPA or certified tax accountant, the deadline may extend by one month to April 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-declaration surcharge of 20% of the final unpaid corporate tax, under-declaration surcharge of 10%, and daily late-payment interest of 0.022% per day; chronic non-filing may lead to tax lien, forced collection, business registration cancellation, and criminal penalties for evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surcharge return and payment equal to a percentage of the central corporate tax payable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local municipality (si, gun or gu) where the head office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, file by April 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing and under-reporting surcharges of 20% and 10% respectively, plus daily late-payment interest of 0.022%; continued delinquency triggers local tax seizure and forced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax (VAT) return and payment for the first and second half of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half (January-June): file July 1-25. Second half (July-December): file January 1-25 of the following year. Digital PropTech SaaS supplies may require cross-border VAT treatment and electronic tax invoices.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT late filing and payment surcharges under the Value-Added Tax Act, including daily interest and additional penalties for failure to issue or report electronic tax invoices; prolonged non-compliance triggers tax assessment and business registration cancellation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary general meeting of shareholders with approval of annual financial statements and retention of signed minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; minutes must be retained at the registered office; registered changes, if any, must be filed with the local court registration office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary general meeting must be convened within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31. Notice must be given at least 2 weeks before the meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible directors may be subject to a non-criminal fine under the Commercial Act for failure to hold the ordinary general meeting within the statutory period; persistent failure to maintain a functional registered office may lead to a court-ordered judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report and submission of the audited financial statements to the financial regulator when audit is mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS); listed companies additionally file through DART electronic disclosure.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed before presentation to the ordinary general meeting; the audited report must be submitted to the FSS within 2 weeks after presentation to the ordinary general meeting, and the OGM itself must be held within 3 months of fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or failing to submit an audit report when required under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies may result in regulatory sanctions, fines, and penalties; the financial statements may be rejected for corporate tax purposes and responsible officers may be prosecuted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of statutory registers and filing of any changes to registered corporate information, including directors, representatives, share transfers or capital changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's statutory registers at the registered office; registered changes are filed with the Korean court registration office having territorial jurisdiction over the head office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Directors, auditors and registered representative changes must be registered within 2 weeks of the change. Share transfers must be entered in the company's shareholder register without undue delay; there is no annual UBO filing in Korea for a private Chusik Hoesa.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register a change of representative or director within 2 weeks triggers a non-criminal fine under the Commercial Act and may prevent the company from asserting the new representative's authority until registration; failure to maintain statutory registers can result in fines and evidentiary disadvantages in litigation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a statutory independent CPA audit is mandatory when a Chusik Hoesa meets any of the following: (a) total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million) as of the end of the preceding fiscal year; (b) it is a listed company or a public company required to submit business reports under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act; or (c) it is expressly designated by the Financial Services Commission because of public interest or investor protection concerns. There is no separate headcount threshold under the Korean external audit rules; turnover is not a general standalone trigger, although high-revenue financial or platform companies may be designated by the FSC on a case-by-case basis.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed and financial companies; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) for unlisted companies subject to external audit unless they voluntarily adopt K-IFRS; small and medium unlisted companies may apply Korean SME Accounting Standards. All statutory audits must be performed under Korean Auditing Standards issued by the FSS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not currently maintain a standalone annual UBO filing requirement for private Chusik Hoesa. Banks and financial institutions perform customer due diligence and periodically refresh beneficial ownership information. For any share transfer, the company must update its shareholder register; if a registered director or statutory representative changes, the company must file an amendment registration with the Korean court within 2 weeks. A shareholder becoming a 5% or greater owner of a listed Korean company is separately required to report the holding within 5 days under capital markets rules. The company must keep the shareholder register and corporate book maintained and available for inspection at its registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Statutory Auditor and Audit Committee Members

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per annum for a mandated or voluntary certified audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top corporate income tax rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local income tax surcharge on assessed corporate tax, producing a 26.4% effective top statutory burden.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible PropTech and SaaS operators may claim the Korean R&D tax credit (up to 25% of qualifying R&D expenditure, with super credits for high-risk technologies), tax incentives for new growth engine technologies and national strategic technologies, and Free Economic Zone (FEZ) tax incentives, including 100% corporate tax exemption for up to 3 years and 50% for the following 2 years for qualifying direct investment enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement) prescribed under the Framework Act on Taxation and the Corporate Tax Act, filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax system (www.hometax.go.kr), including attached financial statements, tax adjustments schedules, foreign tax credit details, and transfer pricing documentation forms.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; however, corporations whose prior fiscal year tax base exceeded KRW 100 million must also file semi-annual preliminary corporate tax prepayment returns and payments within two months after the end of each six-month period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate tax return must be filed within 3 months from the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year entities, the statutory deadline is 31 March of the following year. An extension of up to 1 month is available for medium-to-large enterprises in prescribed circumstances, and separate deadlines apply for foreign-invested companies with an approved business plan.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity identification: corporate legal name, tax identification number (business registration number), representative director details, head office address, and corporate registered address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Korean tax identification number of the Chusik Hoesa. If the company has a branch, permanent establishment, or representative office in Korea, disclose the PE registration and foreign corporate identification. Non-resident shareholders need not be listed in this box, but their names and tax residence countries must be disclosed in the shareholders register attachment to enable withholding tax treaty eligibility checks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year and accounting period: start date, end date, and number of months in the taxable year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the basis period matches the financial statements. For a newly incorporated entity or upon merger, use a short tax period as permitted by law. Cross-border SaaS subsidiaries must reconcile the Korean fiscal year with the parent group's consolidation period and clearly flag any mismatch in the related-party transaction attachment to avoid transfer pricing comparability challenges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income and total sales: report gross revenue under Korean GAAP or K-IFRS, including SaaS subscription fees, software license royalties, implementation service fees, and any rental or property-management related fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all worldwide income of the Korean resident corporation. Non-resident source income from foreign customers is taxable in Korea unless a foreign tax credit is available. Do not reduce gross receipts by platform payment processing fees, gateway charges, or intercompany commission; those items must be claimed as deductions in later adjustment boxes. Any revenue that, under the substance-over-form doctrine, belongs to a Korean permanent establishment or economic employer must be declared here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income and tax-exempt items: dividends received that qualify for the capital-and-profile method, government subsidies eligible for deferred recognition, and exempt fees under special tax incentive legislation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-controlled digital enterprise, avoid over-claiming exemptions on foreign dividend income unless the Korean lower-tier anti-deferral rules are satisfied. Specifically, passive foreign CFC income may be taxed in Korea even if not distributed, so conduct a controlled foreign company assessment and attach the CFC schedule before claiming an exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income adjustments: add-backs and deductions applied to book income to arrive at corporate tax base, including depreciation adjustments, entertainment expense limitation, bad debt allowances, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer pricing adjustments imposed by foreign parent tax authorities must be symmetrically disclosed in Korea. Intercompany royalties for use of software IP, trademarks, and algorithms must be supported by economic analysis using an approved arm's-length method. If the Korean entity is the tested party and recognizes residual profit, clearly report the selected profit-level indicator and benchmark range in the attached Local File. Failure to make proper adjustments will result in a deemed upward adjustment and additional tax at statutory rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign income earned and foreign tax credit: listing foreign-source income classified by country and the foreign income tax paid or accrued.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete country-by-country and item-by-item separate foreign tax credit schedules. For SaaS subscription income sourced to a foreign PE, ensure that the foreign tax qualifies as an income tax under the relevant tax treaty and is not a turnover tax. Carryforward of unused foreign tax credit is limited to 10 years. Non-resident investors holding Korean equity interests should not report foreign taxes in this box; their withholding is governed by the Article 98 corporate tax withholding schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident shareholders and dividend distribution declaration: foreign shareholder identities, tax residency, shareholding percentages, and any treaty-reduced withholding rate requested.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the application for tax exemption or reduced tax under a bilateral tax treaty, accompanied by a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's resident state. If the non-resident shareholder is a private equity fund, composite entity, or special purpose vehicle with pass-through characteristics, obtain a written beneficial ownership declaration and, where required, a treaty-limitation-on-benefits clause compliance statement. The Korean company as withholding agent must secure this documentation before paying dividends; otherwise, the statutory 22% withholding tax applies and non-compliance penalties may be assessed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party international transactions and transfer pricing schedules: report intercompany purchases, sales, royalty payments, interest payments, management fees, and service charges with foreign related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the aggregate value of international related-party transactions exceeds KRW 10 billion in a fiscal year, attach the Korean Local File and Master File. Where the global consolidated group revenue exceeds KRW 1 trillion, attach the Country-by-Country Report notification form. Provide functional, asset, and risk analysis for the PropTech platform, clearly identifying which entity owns development intangibles, which performs core income-generating activities, and which assumes market or credit risk. Transactions without economic substance may be recharacterized under the substance-over-form doctrine.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties are imposed at 20% of the underpaid tax when the return is filed more than 6 months after the statutory due date, with a schedule of lower percentages for less-delayed filings. In addition, unpaid corporate tax accrues a daily overdue surcharge of 20% per annum computed on the unpaid amount. Underreporting or overstating tax bases involves an additional 10% to 40% negligence penalty. Deliberate fraudulent concealment crosses criminal thresholds under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, carrying imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to 3 times the evaded tax; for aggravated offenses, imprisonment may exceed 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on cash or in-kind dividends paid to non-resident corporate or individual shareholders, comprising 20% corporate tax withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge, unless reduced by an applicable bilateral Double Tax Treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the Korean distributing company must: (1) obtain on or before the payment date a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign shareholder's tax authority certifying treaty residence; (2) confirm that the shareholder is the beneficial owner, not a nominee, conduit, or agent; (3) complete and file the 'Application for Exemption from or Reduced Tax under Tax Treaties' (Form 50) through HomeTax before or at the time of withholding; (4) provide a shareholder ownership structure and duration of shareholding schedule where the treaty contains a limitation-on-benefits or abuser clause; (5) maintain contemporaneous evidence of substance, business purpose, and real economic activity of the foreign shareholder for at least 5 years; and (6) if over-withholding occurred, file a refund claim with the competent tax office within 3 years from the statutory payment date. The beneficial owner must not have predefined arrangement or obligation to pass the income to another person, especially a resident of a third country without treaty entitlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates are 22% for both interest and royalty remitted to non-resident enterprises (20% plus 2% local surcharge). Under Korea's bilateral treaties, interest rates are commonly reduced to 10% or 15%, and royalties may be reduced to 0%, 5%, 10%, or 15% depending on the treaty and whether the royalty is for industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment, copyright of software, or patents and know-how. A Korean payor must verify the treaty's 'royalty' definition and the active business clause before applying reduced rates. Payments for cloud-based software and SaaS subscriptions must be classified carefully as royalties or business profits; if the non-resident provider has no Korean permanent establishment, such business profits may be exempt from Korean tax under most treaties, whereas royalties for the right to use copyrighted software code may be taxable at the treaty royalty rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion in aggregate international related-party transactions in a fiscal year triggers mandatory Korean Local File and Master File contemporaneous documentation. Additionally, a Country-by-Country Report is mandatory where the ultimate parent group has annual consolidated revenue of at least KRW 1 trillion. The required documents include entity charts, transactional master file, local country documentation, functional analysis, benchmark evidence, and financial projections demonstrating arm's-length pricing.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) framework comparable to the UAE, but Korean courts and the National Tax Service rigorously enforce the substance-over-form doctrine, the general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) under the Framework Act on Taxation, and the 'core income-generating activities' (CIGA) analysis in international tax treaty and transfer pricing cases. For a PropTech SaaS platform, CIGA in Korea generally includes software development, data and algorithm management, customer contract execution, credit and fraud risk management, and supervision of key outsourced functions. A Korean entity that only holds title, invoices, or receives fees without performing these controlling functions and assuming significant risk will be recharacterized, and treaty benefits may be denied where the beneficial owner lacks substance in its claimed residence state.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-declaring SaaS subscription revenue by diverting customer payments to a non-resident association entity, fabricating intercompany service invoices without actual performance, inflating software development costs, or omitting revenue from the sale of real estate data and tenant screening analytics.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, a violation is punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to 3 times the amount of evaded tax; where the tax evaded exceeds a benchmark serious amount and is planned, the term can be aggravated. Additionally, the National Tax Service may impose a 40% fraud negligence penalty, plus daily late-payment surcharges, and may reject or revise refunds for prior years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts will pierce the corporate veil under the Korean Commercial Act Article 401 and general tort principles where directors use the company as a sham vehicle. Directors who participated in or instructed the false reporting are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax, penalties, and surcharges. They face criminal imprisonment, asset seizure, and blacklisting through the National Tax Service's delinquent payer system, which imposes travel bans at Incheon and Gimhae International Airports. The director's personal bank accounts, real estate, vehicles, and receivables are subject to compulsory execution within the statuted collection period.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Double Tax Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a low-substance non-resident holding company in a treaty jurisdiction to hold Korean equity or receive dividends, royalties, or interest, while the holding company has no employees, premises, authority, or economic activities, and its sole purpose is to obtain treaty-reduced withholding rates on repatriated profits and to disguise the true principal as a third-country entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Korea's general anti-abuse rule and judicial substance-over-form doctrine allow the tax authority to disregard the intermediary entity, reclassify the beneficial owner as the underlying non-resident principal, and reassess the full 22% withholding tax, plus additional 10% to 40% negligence penalties and daily late-payment surcharges. The foreign vehicle may also be denied treaty entitlement under limitation-on-benefits provisions and the OECD Multilateral Instrument principal purpose test (PPT).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the Korean Chusik Hoesa who knowingly participate in treaty abuse may be deemed obligated to have withheld and paid the tax under Articles 98 and 99 of the Corporate Tax Act. They are personally liable for the uncollected withholding amount where they knew or should have known that the beneficial owner requirement was false. They may face a travel ban, extraditable investigation, and imprisonment under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act for aiding and abetting fraudulent claims. In aggravated cases, civil liability for losses of minority shareholders and creditors can be asserted on a joint and several basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging abusive artificial royalties or management fees to Korean PropTech operations, using inconsistent profit-level indicators that allocate systematically all or most residual profit to a low-tax jurisdiction, failing to prepare and deliver the Korean Local File and Master File despite crossing the KRW 10 billion transaction threshold, and carrying out intercompany loans with non-arm's-length interest rates that are effectively unresolved related-party debts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs, the National Tax Service may make a transfer pricing adjustment to the Korean entity's arm's-length income and apply an additional 10% underpayment penalty on the adjusted tax. Failure to submit contemporaneous documentation can result in a separate administrative fine up to KRW 200 million, and the burden of proof shifts to the taxpayer, severely restricting counterarguments. In addition, denial of interest deduction applies to excessive related-party debt under the thin capitalization regime, triggering 22% withholding on deemed dividends on the excess portion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false or incomplete transfer pricing documentation face personal liability under the commercial code for gross negligence. They may be barred from leaving Korea until payment of the adjusted tax is settled, and their personal assets can be attached for restitution. Where the transfer pricing conduct is found to be a deliberate evasion scheme under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, senior officers may be criminally prosecuted and imprisoned for up to 5 years, and a criminal fine up to 3 times the adjusted tax may be imposed. Overseas directors are likewise subject to red flag cooperative extradition requests where an Interpol notice is issued.
